title: Tenant Local Connector delegated execution and typed provider errors

phases.objective: Prove a valid tenant User JWT can execute a tenant-scoped Local Connector proxy request without admin backend-key escalation and expose stable connector error classes without leaking credentials.

e2e_journeys.actor: Authenticated tenant user with a scoped Local Connector device
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A valid delegated tenant request reaches a process-local connector and errors are typed as missing_credential, invalid_credential, denied_scope, timeout, rate_limited, upstream_5xx, invalid_upstream_response, or operation_failure without exposing connector secrets.
steps: Authenticate through the production mixed backend-key/User-JWT middleware using a valid tenant User JWT.
Resolve the exact tenant/user device config from a process-local fake database and forward to a process-local connector HTTP server.
Verify a valid per-device connector credential produces a successful browser response without admin_backend_api_key_required.
Exercise missing and rejected connector credentials, denied scope, timeout, rate limit, upstream 5xx, malformed upstream response, and operation rejection.
Verify each failure exposes a stable connector_error.class and no secret value.
assertions: Valid tenant delegated dispatch succeeds without backend/admin identity.
Missing connector auth is typed missing_credential before dispatch.
401 and 403 connector responses distinguish invalid_credential from denied_scope.
Timeout, rate-limit, upstream 5xx, malformed response, and operation failures have stable typed classes.
All upstream 5xx responses are route-level failures rather than being marked as successful routes.
Connector secrets are absent from tenant error envelopes and attempts metadata.
No live database, local device, provider, Production, secret-store, migration, or external mutation occurs.
